---
title: "Knowledge Mobilization"
---


Excellent science has its greatest impact when it informs decisions.

My research is designed not only to advance scientific understanding but also to support governments, Indigenous communities, industry, non-governmental organizations, and international bodies in addressing the challenges facing the ocean. I work closely with partners throughout the research process to ensure that scientific evidence is relevant, accessible, and useful for policy and practice.

---

## International Assessments

I contribute to major international scientific assessments that synthesize the best available evidence for global decision-making.

These include:

- Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
- Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES)
- United Nations initiatives on sustainable oceans and biodiversity

These assessments provide independent scientific advice that supports governments worldwide.

---

## Working with Decision Makers

Many research projects are developed jointly with government agencies, international organizations, NGOs, and industry partners.

Rather than communicating results only after research is completed, I seek to co-produce knowledge by engaging partners throughout project design, implementation, interpretation, and application.

---

## Tools for Decision Support

My research develops practical tools that help evaluate future risks and opportunities under climate change.

These include:

- Marine ecosystem models
- Fisheries and food security assessments
- Climate risk analyses
- Future scenarios and storylines
- Biodiversity and conservation planning tools

These approaches help decision-makers explore alternative futures and evaluate adaptation options before major changes occur.

---

## Public Engagement

I regularly communicate scientific findings through invited lectures, public presentations, media interviews, and workshops.

I believe that improving ocean sustainability requires dialogue among scientists, policymakers, practitioners, Indigenous knowledge holders, industry, and society.

---

## Selected Partners

Research has been conducted in collaboration with organizations including:

- United Nations agencies
- Fisheries and Oceans Canada
- Environment and Climate Change Canada
- World Wildlife Fund
- Conservation organizations
- National and regional governments
- Universities and research institutes worldwide

---

## From Knowledge to Action

The goal of knowledge mobilization is not simply to communicate research results—it is to enable better decisions.

By combining scientific excellence with collaboration and engagement, I aim to contribute to resilient marine ecosystems, sustainable blue food systems, and evidence-informed ocean governance.
